packet.source:
A queue stores items in first-in, first-out order, abbreviated FIFO. Enqueue adds an item at the back. Dequeue removes and returns the item at the front. Peek returns the front item without removing it. We write queue contents from front to back in square brackets. The queue [A, B, C] will return A on the next dequeue, not C. The order of insertion determines this behavior, not alphabetical order.

Start with an empty queue. Enqueue A, enqueue B, and enqueue C produce [A, B, C]. A dequeue returns A and leaves [B, C]. Enqueue D then gives [B, C, D]. Peek returns B and leaves the same three items. A further dequeue returns B and leaves [C, D]. Distinguish an operation's returned value from the collection remaining afterward; they answer different questions.

In this lesson items have distinct identifiers and the queue has enough capacity for every stated operation. If dequeue or peek is requested on an empty queue, the operation reports empty and leaves the queue unchanged. It does not invent an item or silently reuse the most recently removed one. All worked sequences specify the initial queue and every operation, so there is no hidden earlier state.

A FIFO waiting queue can organize a single server. Assume one task is served at a time, tasks run to completion without interruption, and service begins immediately whenever the server is free and a task is waiting. Arrivals join the back of the waiting queue. A task currently being served is no longer in the waiting queue. When several arrivals share a time, use their stated input order. Durations and arrival times use the same time unit.

For example A arrives at time 0 and needs 4 units of service. B arrives at time 1 and needs 2; C arrives at time 2 and needs 1. A starts at 0 and finishes at 4. B waits from 1 to 4, starts at 4, and finishes at 6. C starts at 6 and finishes at 7. Their waiting times before service are 0, 3, and 4. C is shorter than B, but FIFO does not move it ahead of an earlier arrival. At time 3, A is in service and the waiting queue is [B, C].

For tasks in FIFO order, start time is the larger of arrival time and the previous task's finish time; finish time equals start plus service duration. This also handles idle time: a new task arriving at 10 after the server became free at 7 starts at 10, not at 7. Waiting time is start minus arrival, whereas total time in the system is finish minus arrival. State these quantities separately. The lesson's conclusion is service order under a specified policy, not a claim that FIFO minimizes every possible performance measure.

Peek returns the front item without removing it. We write queue contents from front to back in square brackets. The queue [A, B, C] will return A on the next dequeue, not C. The order of insertion determines this behavior, not alphabetical order.

Start with an empty queue. Enqueue A, enqueue B, and enqueue C produce [A, B, C]. A dequeue returns A and leaves [B, C]. Enqueue D then gives [B, C, D]. Peek returns B and leaves the same three items. A further dequeue returns B and leaves [C, D]. Distinguish an operation's returned value from the collection remaining afterward; they answer different questions.

In this lesson items have distinct identifiers and the queue has enough capacity for every stated operation. If dequeue or peek is requested on an empty queue, the operation reports empty and leaves the queue unchanged. It does not invent an item or silently reuse the most recently removed one. All worked sequences specify the initial queue and every operation, so there is no hidden earlier state.

A FIFO waiting queue can organize a single server. Assume one task is served at a time, tasks run to completion without interruption, and service begins immediately whenever the server is free and a task is waiting. Arrivals join the back of the waiting queue. A task currently being served is no longer in the waiting queue. When several arrivals share a time, use their stated input order. Durations and arrival times use the same time unit.

For example A arrives at time 0 and needs 4 units of service. B arrives at time 1 and needs 2; C arrives at time 2 and needs 1. A starts at 0 and finishes at 4. B waits from 1 to 4, starts at 4, and finishes at 6. C starts at 6 and finishes at 7. Their waiting times before service are 0, 3, and 4. C is shorter than B, but FIFO does not move it ahead of an earlier arrival. At time 3, A is in service and the waiting queue is [B, C].

For tasks in FIFO order, start time is the larger of arrival time and the previous task's finish time; finish time equals start plus service duration. This also handles idle time: a new task arriving at 10 after the server became free at 7 starts at 10, not at 7. Waiting time is start minus arrival, whereas total time in the system is finish minus arrival. State these quantities separately. The lesson's conclusion is service order under a specified policy, not a claim that FIFO minimizes every possible performance measure.

visibleStudy.explanation: 队列按先进先出顺序存储项目。enqueue在队尾添加，dequeue移除并返回队首，peek返回队首不移除。我们用方括号从首到尾书写队列。例如初始空，enqueue P、enqueue Q得到[P, Q]；dequeue返回P并留下[Q]；再enqueue R得到[Q, R]；peek返回Q且队列不变。插入顺序决定下次dequeue，而非字母序。
在单服务器调度中，FIFO等待队列决定服务顺序。任务到达时加入队尾；服务器空闲且队列非空时立即服务队首，正在服务的任务不在等待队列中。例如任务U到达时间0需3单位，任务V到达时间1需2单位，则U先服务(0-3)，V在队列[V]等待至3开始、5结束。到达顺序（非时长）决定离开顺序，短任务V不能越过早到任务U。
结合基本操作可预测执行序列后的队列状态。下面用一个新案例检验：初始空队列，依次执行 enqueue K, enqueue L, dequeue, enqueue M, peek。我们跟踪每一步队首与内容变化。
边界情况：对空队列执行dequeue或peek时，操作报告empty，队列保持不变，不返回项目也不复用已移除项目。例如初始空队列执行dequeue，仍为空[]且报告empty；之后enqueue N得到[N]。这与非空队列行为不同，需明确区分。
visibleStudy.contrast: 若误以为空队列dequeue会返回最近移除的项目，则上述enqueue N前队列会错误地保留该项；实际规则明确不发明项目。

visibleStudy.explanation: 在单服务器 FIFO 调度中，等待队列的 dequeue 对应任务开始服务：它移除并返回队首任务，而剩余等待队列不含该任务；peek 返回队首任务但不改变队列。下面用新案例跟踪：初始等待队列已有 [T1, T2]（T1 最早到达），此时新任务 T3 到达并入队尾。我们逐步观察操作对返回值和剩余队列的影响。

process.startingState: 初始等待队列 [T1, T2]；服务器空闲，即将服务 T1。新任务 T3 到达。
process.ruleOrProcedure: FIFO：dequeue 移除并返回队首；enqueue 加队尾；peek 返回队首不移除。服务开始即 dequeue 等待队列。

steps.action: 执行 dequeue 开始服务 T1
steps.reason: 队首 T1 移除并返回 T1
steps.resultingState: 等待队列变为 [T2]；返回 T1

steps.action: 执行 enqueue T3
steps.reason: 新任务到队尾
steps.resultingState: 等待队列变为 [T2, T3]

process.result: peek 返回 T2 且队列不变；随后 dequeue 返回 T2，剩余 [T3]
process.whyResultFollows: peek 不改变队首，队首仍为 T2；后续 dequeue 移除队首 T2 并返回，留下 T3

activity.prompt: 已执行 dequeue T1 后等待队列 [T2]，接下来 enqueue T3、peek、dequeue 开始服务队首。最终 dequeue 返回的任务及剩余等待队列是什么？
activity.feedback: 正确。peek 后队首仍为 T2，dequeue 移除 T2 返回 T2，剩 T3。
activity.debrief: FIFO 保证队首不变直至被 dequeue，peek 不影响队列内容。

transfer.changedCondition: 若服务器在 T1 完成前 T3 已到达且规则改为优先级调度（非 FIFO），队首可能变为 T3
transfer.prompt: 在上述变更下，enqueue T3 且 T1 仍在服务时，peek 返回什么？
transfer.feedback: 正确，优先级调度下新到高优先级 T3 可能成为队首。
transfer.debrief: 变更调度规则改变了队首确定机制，不再由到达顺序单独决定。

task.prompt: 初始队列 [A, B]。依次执行：dequeue（返回值未记录），enqueue C，dequeue（返回值未记录），peek（返回 C）。最终剩余队列为 [C]。问第一次 dequeue 返回了什么？

result.reasoning: 初始队列 [A, B] 中 A 在队首。根据 FIFO 规则，第一次 dequeue 移除并返回队首 A，剩余 [B]。随后 enqueue C 得 [B, C]；第二次 dequeue 返回 B 剩 [C]；peek 返回 C 且队列不变，与题设最终 [C] 及 peek 返回 C 一致。故第一次 dequeue 返回 A。

通过一个含同时到达的案例演练计算步骤。规则同前：开始=max(到达,上一完成)，完成=开始+服务。下面给出具体任务与已算出的首步，其余由学习者推演。

process.startingState: 空队列，单服务器FIFO：一次一个、运行至完成、同时到达按输入序M然后N。M到达2服务4，N到达2服务2，O到达5服务1。
process.ruleOrProcedure: 开始时间=max(到达时间,上一任务完成时间)；完成时间=开始+服务时长；等待时间=开始-到达。

steps.action: 计算M开始与完成
steps.reason: M最早到达2且服务器空闲，开始=max(2,0)=2，完成=2+4=6
steps.resultingState: M开始2完成6；N已在队列等待；O尚未到达

activity.prompt: 基于上述M的计算与规则，O的开始时间是？

task.prompt: 基于上述M的计算与规则，O的开始时间是？

result.reasoning: M开始2完成6；N同到但列后，开始=max(2,6)=6，完成=6+2=8；O到达5，开始=max(5,8)=8。故O开始时间为8，对应选项A。

packet.source:
A queue stores items in first-in, first-out order, abbreviated FIFO. Enqueue adds an item at the back. Dequeue removes and returns the item at the front. Peek returns the front item without removing it. We write queue contents from front to back in square brackets. The queue [A, B, C] will return A on the next dequeue, not C. The order of insertion determines this behavior, not alphabetical order.

Start with an empty queue. Enqueue A, enqueue B, and enqueue C produce [A, B, C]. A dequeue returns A and leaves [B, C]. Enqueue D then gives [B, C, D]. Peek returns B and leaves the same three items. A further dequeue returns B and leaves [C, D]. Distinguish an operation's returned value from the collection remaining afterward; they answer different questions.

In this lesson items have distinct identifiers and the queue has enough capacity for every stated operation. If dequeue or peek is requested on an empty queue, the operation reports empty and leaves the queue unchanged. It does not invent an item or silently reuse the most recently removed one. All worked sequences specify the initial queue and every operation, so there is no hidden earlier state.

A FIFO waiting queue can organize a single server. Assume one task is served at a time, tasks run to completion without interruption, and service begins immediately whenever the server is free and a task is waiting. Arrivals join the back of the waiting queue. A task currently being served is no longer in the waiting queue. When several arrivals share a time, use their stated input order. Durations and arrival times use the same time unit.

For example A arrives at time 0 and needs 4 units of service. B arrives at time 1 and needs 2; C arrives at time 2 and needs 1. A starts at 0 and finishes at 4. B waits from 1 to 4, starts at 4, and finishes at 6. C starts at 6 and finishes at 7. Their waiting times before service are 0, 3, and 4. C is shorter than B, but FIFO does not move it ahead of an earlier arrival. At time 3, A is in service and the waiting queue is [B, C].

For tasks in FIFO order, start time is the larger of arrival time and the previous task's finish time; finish time equals start plus service duration. This also handles idle time: a new task arriving at 10 after the server became free at 7 starts at 10, not at 7. Waiting time is start minus arrival, whereas total time in the system is finish minus arrival. State these quantities separately. The lesson's conclusion is service order under a specified policy, not a claim that FIFO minimizes every possible performance measure.

visibleStudy.explanation: FIFO模型的一个关键边界是“同时到达按输入序”。若去掉该条件而采用其他排序，则不再是单服务器FIFO假设下所定义的调度。明确该边界可避免把任意排队规则都当作FIFO。
visibleStudy.contrast: 若放弃“同时到达按输入序”而改用最短服务优先，则更短任务可能排在更早到达者之前，这违背了FIFO不重排的假设；资料中的案例里C虽短仍落后于B正是该边界生效的结果。

task.prompt: 假设项目标识不同，队列容量充足，所有操作按给定顺序执行，无隐藏前置状态。初始队列内容为 [U, V]（U 先插入，V 后插入）。依次执行以下操作：1) dequeue；2) enqueue W；3) peek。请回答：(a) 第一次 dequeue 返回什么项目？(b) 执行 enqueue W 后队列内容是什么（用方括号从首到尾书写）？(c) 随后 peek 返回什么项目，此时队列内容是否改变？(d) 用 FIFO 队列的基本操作规则（enqueue 位置、dequeue 与 peek 对队首的作用、插入顺序决定下次 dequeue 而非字母序）简要解释上述结果。

result.reasoning: 初始队列[U,V]队首为U。dequeue移除并返回队首U，剩[V]。enqueue W在队尾加W，得[V,W]。peek返回队首V且不改变队列。符合FIFO：插入顺序定队首，enqueue在尾，dequeue/peek作用于首，peek不修改。
result.answer: (a) 第一次 dequeue 返回 U。(b) 执行 enqueue W 后队列内容为 [V, W]。(c) 随后 peek 返回 V，此时队列内容不改变，仍为 [V, W]。(d) 根据 FIFO 基本规则：enqueue 在队尾添加，故 W 排在 V 之后；dequeue 移除并返回队首，因 U 比 V 先插入（插入顺序决定下次 dequeue，而非字母序），故先移除 U，留下 V 为队首；peek 返回队首 V 但不移除，因此队列保持 [V, W]。
